utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still have some time before we adjourn. Mr. Mundis, as regards the schedule for the rest of the week, can you enlighten us as to what is going to happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I can try. Mr. President, we have one remaining witness for this week, which is the witness whose name appears on the schedule that has previously been provided to the parties and to Your Honours. My understanding is that that witness will not require the full two days and that there will be time remaining on Friday to deal with at least part of the outstanding issues pertaining to the documents. That's about as much enlightenment as I can provide for you today, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then, Mr. Mundis. So tomorrow we are going to have this witness, and on Friday we are going to discuss tendering of documents into evidence. At this stage, would the Defence have anything to raise? Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we do not have anything to raise. The registry has informed us that we will resume tomorrow in Courtroom II. Since the witness is very important, you're aware of his position from the Prosecutor's brief, we are going to try and use only the map. The second thing that I would like to ask you with regard to the position that the witness held in Central Bosnia, the Defence is probably going to ask the Trial Chamber to give them more time than usual. And finally, due to some other commitments that I have in preparation for my defence tomorrow and the day after tomorrow, General Hadzihasanovic will be represented only by my co-counsel, Mr. Bourgon, and our legal assistant. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am also going to give the floor to the other Defence counsel. But before that, I would like to ask Mr. Mundis about tomorrow's witness, for which the Defence said that he's very important. How much time do you think you will need to examine this witness tomorrow? In your list, it says that you have a certain number of documents that you wish to show to the witness. Maybe you're not going to do it, but on your list this is what has been announced.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, my colleague, Mr. Withopf, will be leading the witness tomorrow. My understanding is that he will be proofing the witness, meeting with the witness this afternoon, and consequently, it might be difficult to determine precisely how long or how many documents will be dealt with through the witness. I do know that at the last break, Mr. Withopf had a discussion with at least one of the Defence counsel and indicated he thought he would require somewhere along the lines of 75 to 90 minutes, subject, of course, to his meeting with the witness this afternoon. So I would anticipate at this point that the Prosecution would require one full court sitting, perhaps a little bit more time than that, obviously subject to the discussion that is Mr. Withopf has with the witness this afternoon. But I don't anticipate that that amount of time would be substantially greater than one and a half hours, although it might be slightly more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if the Prosecution takes an hour and a half to two hours, the Defence will have three hours for their cross-examination. We may be able to continue the testimony of this witness on Friday. The Trial Chamber will decide on that after having heard the testimony of this witness. I'm turning to the other Defence counsel. Are there any issues to raise? Who is it who will be leading the cross-examination? Mr. Dixon, can you please indicate approximately how much time will you need for the cross-examination? Just give us a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we estimate at this stage that we will not need longer than 30 minutes for the cross-examination, of course, depending on what is raised by the witness. But our estimate would be no longer than half an hour for our cross-examination tomorrow. And there's nothing else that we wish to raise at this stage, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now on to Friday. Mr. Dixon, you are going to monopolise most of the time regarding these documents. How much time will you need for that? We need to know that in order to decide what to do with the witness who will appear before our discussion on documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will not need longer, as we've indicated before, than one hour to deal with our documents. Hopefully shorter, about 45 minutes, but certainly not longer than one hour. We only have about eight or nine documents to go through. Many of them are documents that will not need to be looked at in much detail, but there are particular points that we wish to refer Your Honours to to raise questions about the reliability of those documents as to whether they should therefore be admitted in the particular categories that we've outlined. But no longer than an hour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you will need an hour, and Mr. Bourgon will have five documents, will need between 20 and 30 minutes, that adds up to one and a half hours. As we have three hours and 45 minutes at our disposal on Friday, we'll have about two hours for the end of the cross-examination and for the Judges' questions, for the witness who is scheduled. So, roughly speaking, this is how we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And naturally, as the Defence will need an hour, Mr. Bourgon will need an hour, and Mr. Dixon 30 minutes, that adds up to an hour and a half, and if necessary, that means that the Prosecution will have time for the re-examination. But the cross-examination of the witness tomorrow, and perhaps on Friday -- the cross-examination of the witness scheduled tomorrow can only continue for two hours on Friday. So I'd like to ask both parties to be very concise so that we can follow this schedule, given that next week we'll have a witness for each day. Are there any other issues to raise? Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no further questions, no further issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will adjourn now, and I will see everyone at the hearing that will start tomorrow at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
